Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
наука
Wikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nauka.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [nɐˈukɐ]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ukɐ
  • Syllabification(key): на‧у‧ка
  • Hyphenation(key): на‧ука

Noun

[edit]

нау́ка • (naúka) f (relational adjective нау́чен)

  1. (uncountable) science (the collective discipline of study or learning acquired through the scientific method; the sum of knowledge gained from such methods and discipline)
    Държа́вата се гри́жи за разви́тието на нау́ката и изку́ството.
    Dǎržávata se gríži za razvítieto na naúkata i izkústvoto.
    The state takes care of the development of science and art.
  2. science, branch of science, discipline (a relatively independent branch of this activity)
    то́чни нау́ки
    tóčni naúki
    exact sciences
    обще́ствени нау́ки
    obštéstveni naúki
    social sciences
    Бъ́лгарска акаде́мия на нау́ките
    Bǎ́lgarska akadémija na naúkite
    Bulgarian Academy of Sciences
  3. knowledge, learning, scholarship, education (knowledge, experience, or education acquired by a person)
    На кого́ се упова́вате? — На мла́дото поколе́ние, кое́то сега́ се въоръжа́ва с нау́ка и съби́ра си́ли за борба́.
    Na kogó se upovávate? — Na mládoto pokolénie, koéto segá se vǎorǎžáva s naúka i sǎbíra síli za borbá.
    Upon whom do you rely? — On the young generation, who are now arming themselves with knowledge and gathering strength for the struggle.
  4. (colloquial, usually in the plural) studies, education, learning
    Дай ми са́мо да оти́да да довъ́рша нау́ките си, да свърша университе́т в Ру́сия.
    Daj mi sámo da otída da dovǎ́rša naúkite si, da svǎrša universitét v Rúsija.
    Just let me go and finish my studies, to graduate from a university in Russia.
  5. (obsolete or dialectal) advice, counsel
    Synonyms: акъ́л (akǎ́l), съве́т (sǎvét), ум (um)
  6. (obsolete or dialectal) moral, lesson, warning
    Synonyms: поу́ка (poúka), поуче́ние (poučénie), уро́к (urók)
    На дру́гите злоче́стиите би́ват нам нау́ка.
    Na drúgite zločéstiite bívat nam naúka.
    The misfortunes of others serve as a lesson to us.
  7. (obsolete or dialectal) habit, custom
    Synonyms: на́вик (návik), приви́чка (privíčka)

Pannonian Rusyn

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak náuka, from Proto-Slavic *nauka. By surface analysis, deverbal from научиц (naučic).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [naˈuka]
  • Rhymes: -uka
  • Hyphenation: на‧ука

Noun

[edit]

наука (nauka) f (relational adjective наукови)

  1. science
  2. (obsolete) teaching
    Synonyms: настава (nastava), ученє (učenje)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of наука (nauka)
singular plural
nominative наука (nauka) науки (nauki)
genitive науки (nauki) наукох (naukox)
dative науки (nauki) науком (naukom)
accusative науку (nauku) науки (nauki)
instrumental науку (nauku) науками (naukami)
locative науки (nauki) наукох (naukox)
vocative науко (nauko) науки (nauki)

Related terms

[edit]
nouns
  • науковец m pers (naukovec)
  • науковка f (naukovka)

References

[edit]

  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “science”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 266

Russian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nauka.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [nɐˈukə]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

нау́ка • (naúka) f inan (genitive нау́ки, nominative plural нау́ки, genitive plural нау́к)

  1. science
    • 1928, Михаил Осоргин [Mikhail Osorgin], “Часть первая. Орнитолог”, in Сивцев Вражек; English translation from (Please provide a date or year):
      Он был изве́стен в учёном ми́ре и свою́ нау́ку люби́л по-осо́бенному; была́ красота́ в его́ нау́ке: окра́ска пе́рьев, пе́нье, приро́да, рожде́нье весны́, проща́ние с ле́том. Поэ́зия была́ в его́ нау́ке.
      On byl izvésten v učónom míre i svojú naúku ljubíl po-osóbennomu; bylá krasotá v jevó naúke: okráska pérʹjev, pénʹje, priróda, roždénʹje vesný, proščánije s létom. Poézija bylá v jevó naúke.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
  2. (figuratively) lesson
  3. Nauka (module of the International Space Station)
  4. Nauka (Soviet and Russian publisher)

Serbo-Croatian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nauka.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /nǎuka/
  • Hyphenation: на‧у‧ка

Noun

[edit]

на̀ука f (Latin spelling nàuka)

  1. (chiefly Bosnia, Serbia, Montenegro) science

Usage notes

[edit]

In Croatia, the more commonly used and preferred literary word is znȁnōst.
